messages:
deploy-bot: :rotating_light: Canary deploy to us-west-2 is reporting elevated 5xx rate for route /v1/generate (prompt-routing=experimental_v2). Error rate jumped to 18% across canary nodes in last 120s. Canary id: canary-20260303-09. Metrics: p95 latency 430ms -> 1.2s, errors 18% (baseline 0.6%). Logs sample attached (truncated).

incident-bot: Pager: @Maya (sre-oncall) — high-severity incident triggered by deploy-bot. Runbook: https://internal/release-runbook#canary-failure.

Maya (sre-oncall): On it. Acknowledging page. Can someone confirm which change landed in canary?

Paul (eng-runtime): That was the prompt-routing refactor + new endpoint variant `prompt_v2` — lightweight routing that rewrites user prompts for output steering. Deployed as canary behind feature flag `flags.prompt_v2` to 5% traffic.

Maya (sre-oncall): Thanks. Do we have request ids or example traces showing the error mode? 5xx or internal assertion?

Paul (eng-runtime): Mostly 500s from runtime kernel: `kv-cache-mismatch` and occasionally OOM during cold-start of shards. Sample log: ```ERROR runtime: kv-cache-mismatch: expected 0x3f, got 0x00 (shard 4)\nstack: ...\n```

Liam (devops): We've already isolated the canary pool: canary-20260303-09 is on g4dn.12xlarge with driver 1.8.2. Rolling it back would require either kill-switch flag flip or immediate canary abort. Which do we want?

Maya (sre-oncall): Risk tolerance low — customer-facing degradation. Activate kill-switch for `flags.prompt_v2` now, then we can evict canary nodes. Paul, can you confirm kill-switch key?

Paul (eng-runtime): Confirmed key: `flags.prompt_v2_enabled` (boolean). API endpoint to toggle: POST https://internal-api.flags.redwood/v1/toggle. Example: ```curl -X POST -H \"Authorization: Bearer $FLAG_TOKEN\" -d '{"key":"flags.prompt_v2_enabled","value":false}' https://internal-api.flags.redwood/v1/toggle```

Liam (devops): I'm going to flip it via the console for speed. Switching to false now.

Liam (devops): done — API returned 200 and propagation started. Console shows target scope: canary/us-west-2 only.

Maya (sre-oncall): Observability — watching error-rate and p95. Sam, please update the on-call support channel and create a customer visibility note for impacted SLAs.

Sam (support): Will do. Drafting note: "We observed elevated errors for a small subset of requests using the experimental prompt routing (prompt_v2). We have disabled the experimental flag and are monitoring. If you experienced a failure please retry; we will follow up." Posting to #customer-comm msgr in 5.

Tanya (product): Any affected customers on Dedicated or Private we need to notify directly?

Paul (eng-runtime): We checked routing: only hosted API traffic in us-west-2 canaries got the flag. No Dedicated or Private tenants received the change.

Rhea (ops-manager): Good. Keep the timeline. After stabilization, plan: roll forward with telemetry fixes or revert code and re-run canary.

Maya (sre-oncall): Error-rate dropping — now 1.2% at p95 back to 380ms. Killing canary nodes to be safe. Liam, please drain and terminate canary-20260303-09.

Liam (devops): Draining now. `kubectl drain canary-20260303-09 --delete-local-data --force` then `aws ec2 terminate-instances --instance-ids i-0abcde` (id masked). Will post when terminated.

Liam (devops): Termination complete. No further 5xx spikes on canary pool.

Maya (sre-oncall): Triage notes for postmortem: root cause likely an incompatibility between prompt_v2 routing transforms and recent KV cache version bump; reproducer on our local sim when running sequence length > 4k. Action items: (1) add integration test for kv-cache versioning, (2) add stricter kill-switch propagation checks, (3) block prompt_v2 rollout until fix. Assign owners? Paul owns (1), Liam owns (2), Paul+Maya for (3).

Paul (eng-runtime): Acknowledged. I'll open the fix PR and tag the postmortem.

Sam (support): Customer note posted. No escalations yet; monitoring channel set to high-alert.

incident-bot: Incident severity set to Sev2. Handoff scheduled: next on-call 18:00 UTC (Maya -> Jordan).

Maya (sre-oncall): Closing incident channel once we've validated stability for 30 minutes. Great job everyone. :thumbsup:
